national_raw_news.content: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved eight railway multitracking projects worth over 20 thousand 800 crore rupees across nine states. The projects will cover around 1,196 km and are expected to improve rail connectivity, ease congestion on existing routes and facilitate faster movement of passengers and freight. They are targeted for completion by 2029-30. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw gave details of the decisions taken by the Union Cabinet during a media briefing in New Delhi today. Mr Vaishnaw said the Cabinet has approved five multitracking projects covering 17 districts across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana. These projects will add about 540 kilometres to the existing Indian Railways network. The total estimated cost of these five projects is more than 10 thousand 21 crore rupees, and they are scheduled to be completed by 2029-30. The projects include the third and fourth lines between Arakkonam and Renigunta, the third and fourth lines between Whitefield and Bangarapet, and doubling of the Hosur-Omalur line. The approved multitracking projects will improve connectivity to around two thousand 100 villages, with a combined population of about 52 lakh. Mr Vaishnaw said the government has also approved three multitracking railway projects at a total estimated cost of more than 10 thousand 700 crore rupees. These projects will cover 14 districts across West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, and will add about 656 kilometres to the existing railway network. The three projects are the fourth line between Kharagpur and Jharsuguda, the fourth line between Katni and Pendra Road, and the third line between Bilaspur and Pendra Road. He said the increased line capacity will significantly improve mobility, operational efficiency and service reliability of Indian Railways. The multitracking projects are also expected to streamline train operations and reduce congestion on busy routes. The Minister further informed that the government has decided to undertake four-laning and quadrupling of all seven high-density railway corridors. These include the four arms of the Golden Quadrilateral, Delhi to Mumbai, Mumbai to Chennai, Chennai to Kolkata, and Kolkata to Delhi along with its diagonals, namely Delhi to Chennai, Mumbai to Kolkata, and then Delhi to Guwahati. Together, these routes cover around 11 thousand kilometres of the railway network. Four-laning of around two thousand kilometres has already been completed. The newly approved projects are part of the government’s efforts to strengthen capacity on the high-density railway network and improve the overall efficiency of rail transportation. In reply to a question on Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train Project, Information and Broadcasting Minister informed that the Bullet train service will commence next year. He said, the construction work on this corridor is progressing rapidly and initally the 100 kilometre section from Surat to Vapi in Gujarat will be open.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 301 India and Sri Lanka sign MoUs on upgradation of L70 Guns and defence cooperation
national_raw_news.content: India and Sri Lanka exchanged Memorandum of Understandings (MoU) on upgradation of L70 Guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force, and cooperation between National Cadet Corps and National Defence Colleges of both the countries. The upgradation of these air defence guns will strengthen the air defence architecture of critical assets in Sri Lanka. The MoU on academic cooperation will facilitate knowledge sharing to further strengthen the academic bonds between them and formalise the NCC youth exchange programme between India and Sri Lanka. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who is on visit to Sri Lanka, today called on President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo and discussed the entire spectrum of the multi-faceted partnership between India and Sri Lanka. During the meeting, both sides reaffirmed that India and Sri Lanka will keep working jointly to ensure the safety, security, peace and prosperity of the region. President Dissanayake reiterated that Sri Lanka would never allow its territory to be used for any activities inimical to India’s security interests. Both sides also reaffirmed that as civilisational twins, close neighbours and maritime partners, they would continue to work together for their development and welfare of the people. . Meanwhile, Both leaders virtually inaugurated three Bailey Bridges constructed by the Indian Defence Forces. During the meeting, Mr Singh conveyed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s warm greetings to Dissanayake. In return Mr Dissanayake also expressed gratitude for the relief assistance provided by India as part of Operation Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah and the comprehensive rehabilitation package extended by New Delhi to facilitate reconstruction and rehabilitation work across different parts of the island. Mr Singh also underlined that the citizens of the two countries share deep friendship based on strong historical and civilisational links and people-to-people exchanges. Mr Singh emphasised that as a closest friend and neighbour of Sri Lanka, India considers it a responsibility to provide assistance as the first responder and would continue to do so in the future. Mr Singh also met Sri Lankan Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya and exchanged views on issues related to development cooperation, education and the close cultural and civilisational ties between India and Sri Lanka. They underlined that as sister democracies with shared heritage, India and Sri Lanka should continue to work on a shared developmental vision for the peace and prosperity of the region.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Sports 200 World Para Archery: Sheetal Devi clinches individual gold; Harvinder & Bhawna win gold in ...
national_raw_news.content: Reigning Paralympics champion Harvinder Singh and world No. 1 Sheetal Devi led the charge as India signed off their World Archery Para Series Stage III campaign in Ahmedabad on a high, winning two gold and four bronze medals, on the final day today. World No. 1 and reigning world champion Sheetal Devi held her nerve in a dramatic shoot-off to win the para compound women’s individual gold, while double Paralympics medallist Harvinder, paired with Bhawna, to clinch gold medal in the para recurve mixed team event. In the recurve mixed team final, double Paralympics medalist Harvinder and Bhawna made short work of China’s Liang Qiurong and Xia Lei, winning 6-nil in straight sets. Bhawna then added another bronze in an all-Indian para recurve women’s bronze-medal play-off, defeating compatriot Rajshree Rathod 6-nil. Sheetal returned in the evening session and produced a composed performance against Kazakhstan’s Aizada Seidan in a thrilling compound women’s individual final. Sheetal, thus, completed a medal double, having earlier teamed up with Toman Kumar to win bronze in the compound mixed team event. India also picked up a bronze in the para compound women’s individual event, with Sarita edging out China’s Wang Huiting. The campaign ended with another bronze for Toman, as the world No. 1 and reigning world champion defeated Iraq’s Abbas Kadhim in the para compound men’s individual event for his second medal of the competition.

national_raw_news.title: India joins group of like-minded governments committed for shaping 6G: Jyotiraditya Scindia 1 hour ago 209
national_raw_news.content: India has endorsed the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, joining a group of like-minded governments that have committed to shaping the sixth generation of wireless communications on the principles of openness, interoperability, security, resilience, resource efficiency and innovation-led competition. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia announced this in a social media post. Mr Scindia said that the global partnership will help accelerate the development of secure 6G wireless networks and coordinate national strategies well ahead of 6G’s expected rollout in the 2030s. The Minister said the initiative complements India’s ongoing work in global standardisation and spectrum fora, as the nation strives to secure 10 percent of global 6G standards. Under the Call to Action, participating governments affirm that secure digital infrastructure is essential to technological competitiveness, economic prosperity and national security, and that advanced telecommunications networks are both the gateway to and the heart of that infrastructure. The initiative also reaffirms that shaping the future of 6G calls for concerted action in collaboration with industry, academia and other stakeholders. The Department of Telecommunications will take forward India’s engagement under the Call to Action and coordinate the relevant follow-up activities with concerned government agencies, industry, academia and other stakeholders. The endorsement was announced on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial, held in North Carolina, United States this month.

national_raw_news.title: National Consumer Helpline facilitates refunds of more than 105 cr rupees at pre-litigation stage 2 hours ago 36
national_raw_news.content: The National Consumer Helpline (NCH) has facilitated refunds of more than 105 crore rupees to consumers across 35 sectors by addressing over one lakh 66 thousand refund-related grievances. These grievances were from the fifteen-month period from 25th April 2025 to 31st July 2026. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the refunds were facilitated at the pre-litigation stage, enabling consumers to obtain timely relief without having to approach the Consumer Commissions. The Ministry noted that the e-commerce sector accounted for the largest share of refund-related grievances, with over one lakh complaints resulting in refunds of more than 74 crore rupees. The Travel and Tourism sector followed, with refunds exceeding 10 crore rupees. The Ministry highlighted that NCH operates through a convergence-based mechanism under which consumer grievances are digitally forwarded to the concerned companies for resolution within defined timelines. It added that refund-related grievances received through NCH have come from metropolitan cities as well as remote regions across the country, reflecting the platform’s reach as a pan-India mechanism for consumer grievance redressal. The Ministry noted that the National Consumer Helpline provides consumers access to grievance redressal in 17 languages through multiple channels. It also encouraged the consumers to proactively utilise the National Consumer Helpline to safeguard their consumer rights and seek redressal of their grievances.

national_raw_news.title: J&K: Three-day annual Kailash Kund Yatra begins in Doda 16 mins ago 5
national_raw_news.content: In Jammu and Kashmir, three-day annual Kailash Kund Yatra began in Bhaderwah town of Doda district today, with devotees embarking on the pilgrimage to seek the blessings of Lord Vasuki Naag. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that amid chants in praise of Lord Vasuki Naag, the yatra passed through Bhaderwah town, where local MLA Daleep Singh Parihar, ADC Sunil Kumar Bhutyal, CEO, Bhaderwah Development Authority (BDA), Sanjeev Sharma and other officers of civil administration, Army, Police CRPF personnel and a large number of locals accorded a warm send-off to the pilgrims. As per the schedule, after a night halt at Hayan (Nalthi), the Yatra would proceed to the Holy destination where devotees will take a dip in the sacred water of Kailash Dal. After performing religious rituals, the Yatra will begin its return journey to Bhaderwah on September 10, 2026. The pilgrimage sees participation from pilgrims hailing from Dudu, Basantgarh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu, Kathua, Udhampur Chenani and Ramnagar, each carrying a Charri Mubarak through different routes to Holy Kailash Kund. The district administration Doda has made elaborate arrangements along the yatra route to ensure the smooth conduct of the pilgrimage. Several officers and medical teams equipped with sufficient medicines and oxygen cylinders have been stationed to provide assistance to pilgrims. Arrangements for drinking water, generator-based electricity, firewood and tents, security have been put in place to ensure the safety and convenience of devotees throughout the yatra. The commencement of the pilgrimage reflects the deep religious faith of the people of Bhaderwah and the region’s rich spiritual traditions.
